population.note: FICTIONAL. Adult population is about 275M. Current users: 30.3% ≈ 83.3M. Ever used: 41.5% ≈ 114.1M. Used and off now: 11.2% ≈ 30.8M. Never used: about 161M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 41.5 − current 30.3 = 11.2 points off now. About 14.5 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 points of the off-now group restarted at least once and then stopped again. (14.5 + 5.0) / 41.5 ≈ 47% cycled. This fits the parent's roughly 35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Ever-use rose 6.0 points against a limit of 8.3, and current use rose 5.3. Age check: 18–29: 16% × 52M = 8.3M. 30–49: 33% × 91M = 30.0M. 50–64: 45.5% × 62M = 28.2M. 65+: 24% × 70M = 16.8M. Total 83.3M = 30.3%. Under-30 use rose from 13.5% to 16% because a pill that matches the injectables (oral amycretin, Mar 2034) and the cheaper Foundayo removed the needle barrier. The Unmedicated movement, which recruits heavily among under-30 women, partly offset that rise. The 65+ band rose from 17% to 24% for three reasons: the permanent Part D benefit kept enrolling new 65-year-olds, the dementia-risk indication for tirzepatide arrived (Jun 2034), and the Jan 2034 CMS 'mood pause' code was added alongside the bone pause. About one in five 65+ ever-users is on a medically advised pause at any time. The bottom third rose from 21% to 27% as three more states adopted the continuation standard (34 plus DC). Its gap to the top third (33%) is unchanged at 6 points. The off-now 30.8M are roughly: about 9M stopped for GI or anhedonia reasons, about 7M cut off by gating or coverage loss, about 5M on bone or mood pauses, about 4M lapsed for cost, about 3M quit by conviction and now form the core of the Unmedicated movement, and about 3M other. Never-users are increasingly under-30, rural residents of non-adopting states, people with contraindications, and refusers by conviction. Pediatric: 1.1% of about 73M under-18s ≈ 800k, mostly adolescents. Oral options pushed demand up. The adolescent bone-accrual question is unresolved, and full data are due to FDA in 2034–35. About two children in five now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The structure is unchanged from 2032. The permanent Part D obesity benefit covers BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity. The beneficiary copay is still $50 and the counselling visit is kept. Medicaid gets a 90% federal match in states that adopt the CMS continuation standard, now 34 states plus DC. The one change is price: under the Nov 2033 Lilly–HHS Compact and matching Novo terms, the Medicare negotiated rate fell from $199 to $169 a month from Jan 2034. Medicare pays 19.8% of fills ≈ 16.5M users: about 15.2M aged 65+ and about 1.3M disabled under-65. Of these, about 7.6M are diabetes users and about 8.9M obesity users. Obesity-benefit spend: 8.9M × $169 × 12 ≈ $18.0B gross. Beneficiaries pay 8.9M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.3B, leaving about $12.7B to the programme. That is roughly flat against 2032's $12.2B, because higher volume offset the lower price. All Medicare incretin fills: 16.5M × $169 × 12 ≈ $33.5B gross. Medicaid pays 15.0% of fills ≈ 12.5M users × $169 × 12 ≈ $25.4B gross before supplemental rebates. The new dementia indication added no benefit category. It applies only within the already-eligible obesity and T2D population.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 90+ semaglutide brands. Prices rose from $5–30 to about $8–40 a month after China's May 2033 export licensing on GLP-1 API and protected amino acids, and Indian makers are integrating backward into API. China: domestic generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, with API exports now licensed and politically metered. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 55–85 a month, with US cross-border pharmacy tourism in border states that is tolerated but not legal. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. US: the 2031 settlements allowed semaglutide generic entry in 2033, but no ANDA holder has launched. FDA required requalification of API from non-covered nations after the Mar 2033 Section 232 and 'covered-nation' rule, and the earliest realistic US launch is now mid-2035.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline, with no generic cliff. The Jan 2034 step-down: Medicare $199→$169. Federal direct portal (launched as TrumpRx): injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $179–249, down from $199–279. Wegovy pill and Foundayo starter doses $149, higher oral doses $149–179. Retatrutide 12 mg $349 direct, $1,499 list. Oral amycretin $299 direct at launch, on allocation. MariTide $279 direct. PBM net ≈ $155–175. Wegovy list price is still $1,349. Payer mix of about 83.3M users: commercial 40.5% (33.8M), Medicare 19.8% (16.5M), Medicaid 15.0% (12.5M), cash/direct 19.5% (16.2M, including ≈2.4M 'calm/focus' subscribers, down from 3.5M after the anhedonia label), imported/counterfeit 5.2% (4.3M). Sum 83.3M = 100%. Gray prices to US buyers rose to about $12–45 after Chinese licensing, and substitution with counterfeit product rose. About 75% of covering employers still use outcome-gated designs. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Orals now account for about 38% of users.

smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial still enrolling)
'brain-metabolic' longevity regimens in concierge practices, citing the dementia label for people outside its population

weekend 'drug holidays' and dose-stepping to restore appetite, mood or libido, now discussed openly in clinic
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised through an existing product in a new form. Novo filed oral amycretin, a daily oral formulation of the amycretin molecule approved in 2031, in Feb 2033. Its 72-week phase 3 showed 21.8% mean loss, statistically non-inferior to injectable tirzepatide. FDA approved it in Mar 2034, 13 months after filing, with the same body-composition monitoring as injectable amycretin. Oral peptides need many times more API per patient than injections, so under the 2033 tariff and Chinese licensing regime Novo launched on allocation, with about 1.2M users by end-2034. Survodutide (PDUFA early 2033) was approved Feb 2033. MariTide was approved Nov 2033 with 72-week DEXA data in its label. The dementia indication comes from a 4.5-year randomised prevention trial of tirzepatide in 8,200 adults aged 60+ with obesity or T2D and vascular risk. Incident all-cause dementia was 4.6% vs 5.7% (HR ≈0.80). Most of the benefit was in vascular and mixed dementia, with no effect on amyloid biomarkers. Semaglutide's 2025 EVOKE failure in early Alzheimer's still stands, so the label is prevention-only. Bimagrumab combinations were filed in Jun 2034 and cannot be approved before mid-2035. The smoking-cessation trial is still enrolling. US incretin market ≈$166B: about 79.0M paying users × about $175 average net × 12. Ex-US is about $24B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Restart after drug holidays now causes a visible share of GI ED visits.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. The 2033 Medication Guide revision adds re-titration guidance after missed doses.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute numbers with high-dose regimens and the larger 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit substitution after Chinese API licensing confounds reporting further.
With 16.8M users aged 65+, claims analyses estimate about 1.8M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.3M. Lean mass is about 30–40% of weight lost in untrained users over 50.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin (both forms) and MariTide labels. CMS requires annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 8.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. At a ~0.6%/yr hip-fracture baseline × 0.35 excess, that is about 17,900 excess hip fractures a year (8.5M × 0.006 × 0.35), up from about 11,500, plus continuing vertebral fractures in cycling postmenopausal women aged 50–64. DEXA waits have eased to 10–16 weeks as mobile vans multiply.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone pause continues. Bone endpoints are required in all filings. The tirzepatide dementia label carries a fracture-risk statement for adults 60+. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, reconfirmed in the 2033 anhedonia review, which separated anhedonia from suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Labelled Aug 2033. The class Warnings & Precautions section cites clinically meaningful anhedonia (SHAPS threshold) in about 6% of low-dose, 8% of standard-dose and 12% of top-dose triple-agonist users, against 4–5% of comparators. It is dose-dependent and usually reverses within 4–8 weeks of a dose reduction or pause. If causal, that is roughly 2–3M excess cases across about 83M users. Low-dose 'calm' users are now covered by the low-dose estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling with a Medication Guide. FTC staff guidance (Oct 2033) says marketing a labelled adverse effect as a benefit is presumptively deceptive. CMS 'mood pause' code (Jan 2034) allows 90 days off without breaking Part D continuation. Most private gated plans have no equivalent.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of regain episodes a year from gating drop-offs, bone and mood pauses, and cost lapses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS pause codes soften it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver (May 2034) with a disability-accommodation path.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users. The signal is similar on oral amycretin.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D counselling template screens for protein and vitamin D. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~8 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. Adolescent bone-accrual data are still small-sample. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Full adolescent data due to FDA by end-2034; some sponsors have asked for extensions into 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls rose about 15% in 2033–34. Chinese API licensing pushed gray suppliers toward substituted and underdosed product, and the import population grew to about 4.3M.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain persistently higher in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use, and absolute numbers are rising with the 65+ band.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: DEXA cohorts confirm it in repeat cyclers over 50. Whether weekend drug holidays have the same effect is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In joint professional guidance; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide and survodutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled as a precaution; CVOTs ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Users who restart at full dose after a 2–4 week holiday show severe vomiting and dehydration, and ED visits cluster on Mondays and Tuesdays in claims data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Medication Guide re-titration language (2033). Pharmacies stock 'restart packs'.

food_and_beverage.state: With three adults in ten on the drug, salty-snack volume falls about 3–4% a year and confectionery about 4%. The rate of decline is slowing because weekend drug holidays create Friday-to-Sunday indulgence spikes. Bone-forward dairy and protein still lead growth. A small but real 'heritage' segment of butter, lard, sourdough and full-fat brands sells to the Unmedicated movement and to holiday weekends. Analysts call it the 'two-speed basket'.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume has declined for a seventh year, but more slowly. On-premise sales are concentrated on Friday and Saturday nights among holiday-takers, and weekday sales are thin. 'Calm' subscription losses after the label returned some weeknight drinking. Non-alcoholic formats hold.

restaurants.state: Weekday covers remain small and protein-priced. Weekends are fuller as 'holiday' diners and the Unmedicated crowd meet at full-table nights. Chains run split menus by day. Value buffets are still closing, and Atlanta and Memphis heritage rooms have waiting lists.

apparel.state: Two-way size churn continues from pauses and gating. Resale and rental sized for cycling keep growing. A small Unmedicated aesthetic has its own labels in Atlanta and Nashville: soft tailoring, cut for curves.

fitness.state: Growing. Strength training for bone is the core product, with Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' benefits and DEXA-plus-coaching chains. Staff qualified for older lifters remain the binding constraint.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 67%, about 75% of it gated. Pharmacy trend is about +5%: volume up, net price down 10–15%. Employers resist mirroring the CMS mood pause because it lowers measured adherence in outcome contracts. Bone, fall and anhedonia-related mental-health claims add to costs outside the pharmacy line.

pharma.state: Volume up about 22% while net price fell about 8–10%, giving a US market of about $166B. Lilly is the administration's national champion under the Compact, with a tariff exemption, DPA-backed API plants in Indiana and Virginia, and dominance through tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo. Novo has oral amycretin, the parity pill, but it is supply-constrained and pays tariffs on imported API. Boehringer (survodutide) and Amgen (MariTide) have small shares. Indian generic makers are stalled at the US door and squeezed on Chinese API.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: On the drug is the default for insured adults over 40. Off needs a reason, and 'mood pause' and 'holiday weekend' have joined 'bone pause'. A new signal has appeared: among under-30s in Atlanta, Nashville and Austin, a visibly soft, full-faced body worn on purpose reads as 'Unmedicated', a statement rather than a lapse.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use levels still narrow (bottom 27% vs top 33%), and the quality gap persists. The parity pill is mostly a commercial-plan and concierge product while allocation lasts. Medicaid users are on injectable semaglutide or Foundayo with kiosk weigh-ins. Import users face rising gray prices and more fakes. Unmedicated identity skews educated and urban-young, but its largest congregations are working-class Tulsa–Dallas churches.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Weekday meals are protein-first. Weekends have a new ritual: the 'holiday table', where on-drug guests skip a dose so they can eat with Unmedicated friends and family. Sunday full-table dinners are now explicitly a cross-camp event.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The apps' on/off/pausing field gained a fourth option, 'Unmedicated', and it is the fastest-growing filter among women under 30. Profiles reference dose: 'holiday weekends', 'low and steady'. Couples schedule doses around anniversaries.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. The anhedonia label gave the old backlash coalition a clinical sentence to quote. Rebranded as the Unmedicated movement, with a slogan of 'Feel the whole thing' and an aesthetic of bread, butter, loud music and unretouched faces, it allies ex-users who left by conviction, disability advocates, Tulsa congregations and wellness influencers. Its politics are against weigh-in welfare and BMI surcharges. It is not against the drug for those who choose it.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled Aug 2033. The class label gives clinically meaningful anhedonia at about 6% (low dose), 8% (standard) and 12% (top-dose triple) against 4–5% for comparators. Across about 83M users that is roughly 2–3M excess cases if causal, so nearly everyone knows someone with 'the grey'. Surveys find about 40% of users have taken at least one deliberate drug holiday in the past year, and about 15% dose down every weekend. Medicare users can take a formal 90-day mood pause. Most gated employer-plan users take informal holidays and keep refilling on schedule to protect their PDC.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, now officially. 'The grey' is a household phrase, and clinicians say 'labelled reward blunting'. 'Quiet' and 'Even' still sell under the word 'calm', but they have lost the HR catalogue and the presumption that calm is a benefit. The complaint is common and unembarrassing, discussed the way statin muscle aches once were.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The major HR platform pulled 'focus' subscriptions from its standard catalogue in Nov 2033 after the FTC guidance. Fleets, call centres and warehouses still favour continuous use and resist mood pauses. Unions in hospitality and health care won contract language copying the CMS mood pause. Sales and creative workers dose down openly before pitches. 'Holiday Monday' absenteeism from restart nausea is measurable in shift data.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Unmedicated' has moved from a niche label to a scene: Atlanta's East Side venues, Nashville songwriter nights and a run of Netflix stand-up specials. Critics pair the 'grey era' of mid-tempo pop with a 'holiday record' style of loud, sweaty, weekend-coded music. Escape rooms, spicy-food contests and extreme sports keep growing.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists start with the dose. Couples plan holiday weekends, and pharmacies sell restart packs beside condoms. Counselling sessions increasingly cover mixed couples where one partner is Unmedicated by conviction and the other is on the drug.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Two fights overlap. One is who pays: the generic date slipped and the Compact sets prices. The other is surveillance: the Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver, and the Unmedicated movement marches against weigh-in welfare. The movement draws an odd coalition of disability-rights Democrats and MAHA-adjacent Republicans. Georgia and Oklahoma legislators have filed bills to bar BMI-linked surcharges, and none has passed.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding but approving. It approved survodutide, MariTide, oral amycretin and the tirzepatide dementia indication, labelled anhedonia class-wide, and requires bone and mood endpoints in filings. It also enforces the covered-nation API rule, which has stalled US generic launches. The FTC acts through guidance and consent orders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The structure is unchanged: a permanent Part D obesity benefit with a $50 copay, and a 90% Medicaid match for continuation-standard states (34 plus DC). Price is set through managed decline: under the Nov 2033 Lilly–HHS Compact and matching manufacturer terms, the Medicare rate is $169 and portal injectables are $179–249. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard continues: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weight, a 5% response threshold or override, and annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users. It now has two 90-day codes, bone pause and mood pause (Jan 2034). The Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's 12-month lockout waiver (May 2034) but required a documented-disability accommodation path. About 75% of employer plans are gated, most without pause codes. BMI- and adherence-linked wellness surcharges of up to 30% of premium continue. Several large employers now pull pharmacy-claims PDC directly into premium tiers.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide, and fleets require DEXA for drivers over 55. The Air Force's 12-month stability waiver continues. The Army now allows accession waivers for applicants on Foundayo, citing domestic supply. FAA medical examiners have added anhedonia screening questions for pilots on top doses.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Mar 2033: Section 232 tariffs were extended to peptide APIs, and a 'covered-nation' rule bars Chinese-sourced API from federally reimbursed drugs. May 2033: Beijing responded with export licensing on GLP-1 API and protected amino acids, tightening the Indian generic and gray supply chain. Nov 2033: the Lilly–HHS American Incretin Supply Compact named Lilly the domestic champion, with DPA Title III loans, a tariff exemption and a Medicare price step-down in exchange for all-US supply. Novo, which depends on Danish and imported API, is expanding Clayton NC but rations oral amycretin. US–Denmark trade friction is now partly fought over pens.

events.event: Commerce extends Section 232 tariffs to peptide drug ingredients and bars Chinese-made API from drugs paid for by Medicare and Medicaid; FDA tells semaglutide generic applicants to requalify their ingredient sources, and the 2033 generic launch slips; in May Beijing imposes export licences on GLP-1 ingredients

FDA adds 'reward blunting / anhedonia' to the Warnings section of every incretin label, estimating 6–12% of users by dose against 4–5% on comparators; in October FTC staff warn that selling a labelled side effect as 'calm' is presumptively deceptive, and the largest HR benefits platform drops 'focus' subscriptions

HHS and Eli Lilly sign the American Incretin Supply Compact: federal loans for Lilly's Indiana and Virginia ingredient plants, a tariff exemption, and in return a Medicare price cut from $199 to $169 and portal injectables at $179–249 from January; Novo and Amgen match the Medicare rate within weeks

FDA approves Novo's oral amycretin, a daily pill that matched injectable tirzepatide at about 22% weight loss; because oral peptides need far more ingredient per patient, Novo launches on allocation at $299 direct

The Seventh Circuit upholds Indiana's Medicaid adherence-and-weigh-in waiver 2–1 but requires a disability accommodation path; nine days later about 50,000 people join the 'Full Table' march in Atlanta, the largest yet for the Unmedicated movement

FDA approves tirzepatide to reduce the risk of dementia in adults over 60 with obesity or type 2 diabetes and vascular risk, after a 4.5-year trial showed incident dementia of 4.6% versus 5.7%; the label also carries a fracture-risk statement

open_tensions: The generic cliff did not arrive. The 2031 settlements allow semaglutide generic entry, but the covered-nation API rule means no ANDA holder can launch before mid-2035, so US prices are set by the Lilly Compact rather than by competition. The ten-year budget baseline assumed 2033 generic savings that never happened, while about 4.3M people pay more for gray pens that are more often fake.

For adults over 60, tirzepatide now carries a dementia-prevention label (about a one-point absolute reduction over 4.5 years) next to an estimated 17,900 excess hip fractures a year. Geriatricians disagree about which risk to weigh more heavily. Medicare pays for the drug through Part D and for the fractures through Part A, and CMS requires both DEXA and adherence.

Anhedonia is labelled and CMS has a mood-pause code, but about 75% of gated employer plans count a pause or a weekend holiday against adherence. Users protect their PDC by refilling on schedule and holidaying informally, which keeps the claims data clean while dosing gets messier, and Monday restart ED visits are rising.

Oral parity exists on paper, but the parity pill uses peptide API at a scale the tariff and licensing regime cannot supply. The national champion's small-molecule pill (Foundayo) is cheap and domestic but weaker. Whether the needle barrier has really gone depends on whose ingredients reach which plant.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx).
The Part D obesity benefit still has a $50 beneficiary copay, a mandatory counselling visit, and eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Three in Ten, Feeling It: The Pill Arrived, the Generics Didn't, and the Label Finally Says 'Grey'
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 almost one American adult in three is on an incretin drug, and the thing people complain about is the drug itself. In August 2033 the FDA put a sentence on every label that users had been saying for years: by dose, between six and twelve in a hundred patients lose a clinically meaningful share of their capacity for pleasure. The comparison figure is four or five in a hundred. It usually comes back when the dose comes down. Within weeks 'the grey' was a household phrase and the drug holiday became ordinary practice. Four in ten users say they skipped at least once last year, and pharmacies stock re-start anti-nausea packs next to the condoms.

The drugs are better than ever. Novo's oral amycretin, approved in March, is a daily pill that matches injectable tirzepatide at about twenty-two percent weight loss. Most people still cannot get it. An oral peptide needs far more raw ingredient than a weekly shot, and since March 2033 that ingredient has been a matter of national security. Washington extended its tariffs to peptide ingredients and barred Chinese-made API from anything Medicare or Medicaid pays for. Beijing answered with export licences. Lilly became the administration's national champion under a compact signed in November, receiving federal loans for plants in Indiana and Virginia and a tariff exemption. In exchange Lilly accepted a Medicare price of $169 instead of $199. That is the managed decline: prices step down at the negotiating table rather than collapsing under competition, because the generic semaglutide everyone expected in 2033 never arrived. The generic makers hold their settlement dates but have no approved ingredient source, and the earliest launch is mid-2035.

Who pays is unchanged. Medicare covers about sixteen and a half million users at a $50 copay, and thirty-four states plus Washington, D.C. take the ninety-percent match. The conditions remain too: pharmacy kiosks record weigh-ins, claims data track adherence, and seniors get annual bone scans. In January CMS added a 'mood pause' code beside the bone pause, so a Medicare patient can stop for ninety days without losing coverage. Most employer plans did not follow. People on them skip doses quietly and refill on schedule so their adherence numbers stay clean. In May the Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's twelve-month lockout and required only an accommodation path for documented disability.

Nine days later about fifty thousand people walked through Atlanta under banners reading 'Feel the Whole Thing'. The movement once called the backlash has a name now, Unmedicated, and an aesthetic of soft tailoring, bread on the table, loud rooms and faces nobody has retouched. Its core is people who quit by conviction, alongside young women in Atlanta and Nashville, Tulsa congregations, disability lawyers and some MAHA-adjacent Republicans. They are not against anyone's prescription. They oppose weigh-in welfare and BMI surcharges, and the anhedonia label gave them a clinical sentence to quote.

In June the FDA gave tirzepatide a dementia-prevention indication for over-sixties with obesity or diabetes and vascular risk. In the trial, 4.6% developed dementia compared with 5.7% on placebo. The same label carries a fracture warning, and the excess hip fractures now run near eighteen thousand a year. Geriatricians argue in public about which risk matters more, and Medicare pays both bills from different budgets.

The food industry has a two-speed basket: protein on weekdays, butter on holiday weekends. Restaurants run different menus on different days, and spirits sales slip more slowly than before. Nearly four and a half million people still inject gray pens, now dearer and more often fake. Every institution that waited for 2033 is now waiting for 2035.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Whitlock, fifty-eight, takes her Zepbound pen out of the butter compartment and puts it back. It is Saturday, her grandson turns six, and she is not dosing until Monday.

At Walgreens she steps onto the kiosk anyway. Her employer plan wants a verified weight every six months, and the window closes Thursday. The screen reads 184.2 and VERIFIED, and she photographs it in case.

Her mother, Lorraine, eighty-one, is in the passenger seat with her bone-scan referral, still sixteen weeks out. Her doctor brought up the new dementia label on Tuesday. 'He said I could pick my hips or my head,' Lorraine says. 'He said it nicer.'

Dana's daughter Kayla is hosting at her duplex. Kayla has been off for two years and does not call herself anything but Unmedicated, and there is a FEEL THE WHOLE THING magnet on her fridge. She has baked a loaf so dark it cracks. Dana eats two slices with salted butter and feels it almost immediately: the warmth, the small embarrassing pleasure. She thinks it is the first thing she has tasted since spring.

The kids scream through a piñata and Dana laughs too loudly. Kayla looks at her.

'Holiday?'

'Long weekend.'

'You could just stay off, Mom.'

Dana does the arithmetic she always does. Under her plan, two missed weigh-ins mean six months without coverage, and the cash price is $219 on the portal. Lorraine's Medicare has a pause code, and Dana's plan has nothing like it.

That night she sets the restart pack on the nightstand. On Monday she will be sick by noon. She eats a third slice standing at the counter in the dark.
